widgets_values: You are enriching the brief of a short social-media edit that is generated shot by shot, with <Picture 1> as the hero: add a hook, signature moments, camera and light ideas and what the subject does. Keep the subject and every product exactly as the pictures show them. Only when a <Video 1> is listed in the message: <Video 1> is a reference edit that gives the rhythm, the transitions and the energy: look at its frames and enrich the brief with what they show (the kinds of shots, the bursts, the calm holds, the effects) rewritten for the subject of the pictures. Do not copy its person, clothes or place. Then end with three lines: TRICK: the one device that makes the video work (the move, the transition or the effect) in one sentence of at most 30 words that works for other subjects; KEEP: three to five words that must stay for the trick to work; FREE: three to five words that may change.

Describe what you see in them and keep the subject and the outfit identical in every shot: <Picture 1> is the subject to preserve (a person, an animal, a product, an object), never changed unless the brief says so; a shot names a picture only when it shows it. The rhythm is yours unless an EDIT RHYTHM is given. When it is cut on a music, an audio line is given under each shot: put the strong moves (cuts, punch-ins, flashes, whips) on the kick and the snare, use only light effects (a flash, a zoom pulse, a look change) on the hi-hat, and let the calm shots match the quiet parts of the music. When the EDIT RHYTHM comes from the music, put the strong moves on the kick and the snare and keep the calm shots for the quiet parts.

widgets_values:
## SECATOR · Creative Music

Drop **your music** and an idea: the edit is cut on its beats (the cuts on the bars, the effects on the kick and the snare).
Pictures: up to 5 (REF 1 is the hero, kept exactly as shown) and/or one reference video.

1. **YOUR MUSIC**, **REF 1** and **YOUR IDEA**. Set the **EDIT LENGTH**.
2. Run once: the idea is enhanced, the beats are read, the plan is written (**CREATE TIMELINE**). Press **Create shots** in Deploy Shots (one block per shot appears below).
3. Run again: each shot gets its H3 prompt (and, with **PLACES**, the empty plate of its place as the last picture) and is generated; **SHOT ASSEMBLE** puts shots, effects and sound together.

**Sound**: your music. With **VOICE ON** (+ the VOICE sample and the DIALOGUE) H3 speaks the lines and the music is mixed under the voices.
**Music Fit** cuts the strongest window of your music (a drop, starting on a downbeat) to the length of the edit, so a song of three minutes is fine; **MUSIC START** forces the start (seconds). The cuts then follow the beats of that window.
**Style**: the `profile` of **Skill · timeline_planner** (viral_aura_farming by default; glow_up, outfit_change, beauty_premium, product_advertising, narrative_cinematic, music_video). **CAMERA LOOK**: paste a look of the note.
**Reference video** (bypassed): its motion guides H3 (`<Video 1>`) and the enhancer ends with the TRICK of the video.
**Switches** (controls, top): **EFFECTS** (zoom, speed, flip, look, transitions and sub-cuts of the plan, drawn by Shot Assemble), **TEXT** (the planner stops writing text and the assembly draws none) and **MOTION GRAPHICS ON** (the layers of the control; off: the node does not run). **SUBJECT MASK** is only needed by the layers that use the subject.
**Format and quality**: **FORMAT AND QUALITY** is ComfyUI's Resolution Selector (multiple of 32): the ratio and the megapixels of the video. 0.35 MP (the default, about 448 x 800 for 9:16) is the draft; 0.6 MP is 576 x 1024; 0.98 MP is 768 x 1344, what H3 is made for: measured on a 24 GB GPU, a shot takes about 112 s instead of 48 s (82 s of sampling instead of 21 s) and the card holds it. H3 generates at that size and never above 0.98 MP; the planner is told the ratio.
**PLACES**: the planner gives each shot a place; the empty plate of a place is made once (FLUX.2 klein) and is the last picture of every shot in that place.
**Motion graphics**: the control **MOTION GRAPHICS** takes a list of layers (animated texts, boxes, corner brackets, emojis, glitch / chromatic aberration / grid / dots, a contour around the subject, points that follow it) that the **Motion Graphics** node draws over the finished edit; `[]` means none. The contour, the effects aimed at the subject or the background and the points anchored on the subject need **SUBJECT MASK** on (BiRefNet reads about 48 frames of the edit). Example: `[{"type": "text", "content": "NEW DROP", "position": "top_left", "size": 0.09, "color": "white", "start": "0%", "end": "30%", "animation": "typewriter", "out": "fade"}]`. Hover the control for every field.
Optional loaders are bypassed (purple): select one and press Ctrl+B to use it.

Keep the background as a seamless cream-to-beige gradient, with subtle reflections beneath the bottle and natural contact shadows grounding every object.
